ba-are-we-fast-yet[bot] opened issue #15342:

are-we-fast-yet found 5 regressions in virtual cycles (callgrind) between Wasmtime b20de21ba40a and be64d1bde395.

The range is the single commit be64d1bde395 GC: implement Unrooted references. (#15191), so it is blamed without bisecting. See the bisect.

  • Baseline: run 00135 (metadata), Wasmtime b20de21ba40a
  • This run: run 00136 (metadata), Wasmtime be64d1bde395

A change counts when a Mann-Whitney U test finds it significant at the 0.01 level and it clears its phase's minimum relative change:

phase geomean individual
compilation 0.3% 1%
instantiation 2.5% 20%
execution 0.5% 2%

Regressions (5)

benchmark phase Δ virtual cycles virtual cycles noise Δ instructions retired instructions retired noise
Geomean execution +0.82% (+0.75% to +0.89%) n/a n/a n/a
rust-wasmprinter/rust-wasmprinter.wasm execution +5.30% (+5.28% to +5.49%) 0.186% -> 0.020% +4.58% 0.004% -> 0.004%
hoot-earley-boyer/hoot-earley-boyer.wasm execution +4.01% (+3.95% to +4.04%) 0.086% -> 0.039% +4.10% 0.001% -> 0.001%
dotnet-raytracer/dotnet-raytracer.wasm execution +2.89% (+2.88% to +2.91%) 0.016% -> 0.025% +1.56% 0.003% -> 0.004%
dart-deltablue/dart-deltablue.wasm execution +2.73% (+2.72% to +2.74%) 0.017% -> 0.017% +2.78% 0.001% -> 0.001%

A positive delta is a slowdown, a negative delta is a speedup.

instructions retired counts work done rather than how well it was predicted. A regression whose instructions didn't move is often Valgrind's branch predictors aliasing on a code layout change; see docs/regressions.md.

Each noise column is how far that event's own counts spread.

Commits

https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/compare/b20de21ba40a67233f68466924b715a42bf557c8...be64d1bde3953ee4404df9f2d9dfd33d2de3fc1a

  • be64d1bde395 GC: implement Unrooted references. (#15191)

Reproduce locally

On x86-64 Linux with Valgrind installed:

git clone https://github.com/bytecodealliance/sightglass
cd sightglass
git checkout 2d453335318d05cf42b6f3263aa68f0021985f10
rustc engines/wasmtime/build.rs -o build-engine
mkdir old new
REVISION=b20de21ba40a67233f68466924b715a42bf557c8 ./build-engine old
REVISION=be64d1bde3953ee4404df9f2d9dfd33d2de3fc1a ./build-engine new
cargo run --release -- benchmark --measure callgrind \
  --engine old/libengine.so --engine new/libengine.so \
  --engine-flags-common="-Cparallel-compilation=n --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -Ccranelift-has-sse3 -Ccranelift-has-ssse3 -Ccranelift-has-sse41 -Ccranelift-has-sse42 -Ccranelift-has-popcnt -Ccranelift-has-avx -Ccranelift-has-avx2 -Ccranelift-has-fma -Ccranelift-has-bmi1 -Ccranelift-has-bmi2 -Ccranelift-has-lzcnt -Ccranelift-has-cmpxchg16b" \
  -- benchmarks/dart-deltablue/dart-deltablue.wasm benchmarks/dotnet-raytracer/dotnet-raytracer.wasm benchmarks/hoot-earley-boyer/hoot-earley-boyer.wasm benchmarks/rust-wasmprinter/rust-wasmprinter.wasm

fitzgen commented on issue #15342:

cc @cfallin

The delta instructions retired looks a little concerning. Possible there isn't much we can do and this is just a consequence of host code that uses Val being a bit more expensive, but seems worth looking into whether there are any cheap mitigations.
